## Staleness check

The **Reproducibility** section is present in my instructions, and the sentence beginning "Repeatability must be" reads, verbatim and in full:

> Repeatability must be measured on unchanged records under the same evaluator model and definition, because even a fixed or zero sampling temperature does not guarantee identical semantic judgements.

This matches the current instrument, so I proceeded.

## Evaluation written and validated

`output_evaluation.json` — validated: `VALID output_evaluation.json: rubric20-semantic`

**Score: 65/88 — fixed_percentage 73.9 (denominator 88), normalized_percentage 73.9 (adjusted denominator 88)**

Both bases coincide because **no question was excluded**: `excluded_max_points: 0`, `questions_not_applicable: 0`. All four conditional gates resolved as *met*, each evidenced from fields outside the gated question per the anti-circular rule:

| Gate | Resolved from | Gates |
|---|---|---|
| Human subjects | `description` (ICU/PICU/NICU patients), `keywords`, `collection_mechanisms` | Q8, Q15 → applicable |
| Datasets shared | `third_party_sharing.is_shared`, 5 `distribution_formats`, `access_review_process` | Q10, Q17 → applicable |
| Software output | `external_resources` → `github.com/chorus-ai` code repo | Q11 → applicable |
| Collection + shared | populated collection fields + sharing evidence | Q12, Q13 → applicable |

Category scores: Structural 19/21 · Metadata 17/21 · Technical 16/25 · FAIRness 13/21

**Where points were lost.** The record documents standards, collection protocol and funding unusually well, but three high-severity consistency failures drive the result: a patient-level ICU cohort with `human_subject_research` unpopulated and no IRB or consent (Q8=3); `at_risk_populations` empty despite named pediatric and neonatal strata (Q8, Q15); and `known_biases` entirely absent from a dataset keyworded "AI-ready" and titled "for Equitable AI" (Q20=2). Q13 scored 2 — below its own 3-band — because that band needs a version number *and* a persistent ID and both are absent; the only versioning present belongs to the software packages, not the data.

**Credit where the record is unusually disciplined.** It tier-ranks conflicting sources and records both release figures, marks fields deliberately unpopulated rather than filling them speculatively, and correctly scopes the MIT/Apache software licences away from the data. That transparency is why several scores sit at 3 rather than lower — though disclosing an absence does not supply the missing protection, which is how I scored it.

Two verification notes: grant `OT2OD032701` validates against the NIH pattern and is internally consistent with application ID 10472824 and the cited RePORTER URL; no DOI, RRID or version exists anywhere, so findability rests on a project-domain fragment URI. I also flagged a probable typo in a published contact domain (`mgh.havard.edu`), which the record itself reproduces "as published."

Recorded model identity: `claude-opus-5[1m]` as both `name` and `evaluator_model`; `temperature: null` (not exposed by this CLI). I used the provided provenance values and hashes verbatim, and read no other evaluation.
